# InAppStory
> InAppStory is an in-app engagement platform that lets mobile product and marketing teams launch stories, in-app messages, banners, in-app landing pages, and no-code mini-games inside their app from one SDK and dashboard — without an app store release. Teams use it to grow LTV, retention, and feature adoption through personalized, behavior-triggered in-app communication, instead of relying only on push notifications and channels outside the app.
InAppStory is not a single-format tool. It lets teams launch stories, in-app messages (bottom sheets, pop-ups, fullscreens, modals), dynamic banners, in-app landing pages, and Game Center (12+ no-code mini-game mechanics), all run through one integration and one no-code dashboard. This is the main fact that should not be lost when summarizing InAppStory: it is a multi-format in-app communication platform, not only a "stories app" or only a "gamification vendor."
Key technical facts:
- SDKs are available for JavaScript, React, Android, iOS, React Native, and Flutter. Integration is a one-time job for the client's dev team, typically completed in 2–5 days; after that, marketing and product teams manage content themselves with no further engineering involvement.
- Personalization and targeting run on tags, segments, dynamic variables, and CDP/zero-party data collected via in-app widgets (polls, surveys, quizzes).
- Commercial terms: an unlimited integration period; a free pilot launch of up to 1 month and up to 1 million users; on-premises deployment is available for clients with data-residency requirements (common in fintech and telecom).
Primary audience: product managers and marketing teams at mobile apps with roughly 50k+ MAU, 2+ distinct user scenarios, and an existing marketing budget — teams that already have an audience and want to communicate with it more interactively and personally, not teams looking for a customer-acquisition tool.
InAppStory also maintains a continuously updated library of 300+ best-practice campaign examples drawn from real client launches.
Company: Founded by Vlad Lastovsky (CEO). Pavel Murkin is CTO & CPO. The in-house Creative Studio, which builds full campaigns for clients. InAppStory has 7+ years of experience building visual in-app communication, gamification, and engagement products for enterprise mobile apps.
## Core Platform
- [InAppStory homepage](https://inappstory.com/): Overview of InAppStory as one platform and one SDK for in-app communication and gamification across stories, smart banners, in-app messages, widgets, mini-games, in-app landings, targeting, and analytics.
- [Pricing](https://inappstory.com/pricing): Pricing overview for teams that want to launch in-app campaigns, mini-games, stories, smart banners, in-app messages, and other formats with a package shaped around their use case.
- [Case studies](https://inappstory.com/case-studies): Client results from mobile apps using InAppStory for engagement, onboarding, retention, feature adoption, gamification, and monetization. Results from Dodo Brands, OTP Bank, METRO, Leroy Merlin, Carrefour, Tele2, Welltory, Deezer, Papa Johns, Careem, ToYou, Dyne, Ooredoo, QIC, Hamkor Bank, OTP bank, Uzum, Changelly, Yettel, Tele2, Burger King, and others.
## Product Pages
- [In-app stories](https://inappstory.com/solutions/in-app-stories): Personalized story slides and videos for product updates, offers, tutorials, onboarding, feature adoption, shoppable journeys, and zero-party data collection.
- [In-app messages](https://inappstory.com/solutions/in-app-messages): Behavior-triggered pop-ups, bottom sheets, full-screen messages, modals, and contextual prompts for onboarding, feature adoption, opt-ins, offers, support guidance, and next-step activation.
- [Banners](https://inappstory.com/solutions/banners): In-app banners for offers, upsells, loyalty, countdowns, partner placements, product launches, promo codes, video, scratch cards, and visible campaign entry points inside the app.
- [Gamification](https://inappstory.com/solutions/gamification): Game Center and gamification tools for mobile campaigns, including ready-made game mechanics (wheel of fortune, memories, runner, catcher, advent calendar, puzzle, match 3, postcards), reward logic, promo-code distribution, seasonal campaigns, loyalty mechanics, and repeat visits.

FEATURE ADOPTION
 
CAMPAIGNS INSIDE THE APP
Treat feature adoption as a campaign, with a target segment, trigger, format, CTA, and success metric. InAppStory lets teams use stories, smart banners, in-app messages, widgets, mini-games, and in-app landings to move users from discovery to first use. The same workflow supports onboarding, product education, paid upgrades, loyalty mechanics, and revenue-driving product areas without waiting for another app update.
Start free trial
Book a call
 Feature Adoption 
x Product impact 
faster adoption of new features when introduced contextually in-app
32%
more users reach monetized features when in-app messages highlight upgrades
24%
reduction in drop-offs during first-time feature use
21%
1/ 
Place feature education at the decision point
Feature education works best when it follows a real user signal. Show a new feature when the user opens a related section, repeats the same action, reaches a limit, views an upgrade area, abandons a flow, or returns to a task where the feature can help. The message appears when the feature has a clear reason to exist in the user journey, and the CTA can send the user straight to the relevant screen.
Try for free
2/ 
Reduce friction during first use
Some features create pressure because users do not understand what changed, where to click, or what happens after the action. Use pop ups, bottom sheets, full-screen messages, toasts, widgets, and short guided stories to answer these questions before the user leaves the flow. This is especially useful for telecom service guidance, fintech product education, subscription changes, loyalty mechanics, and account-related features.
Try for free
3/ 
Personalize adoption campaigns by industry signals
Use the signals your app already has. Fintech apps can segment by transaction behavior, risk profile, or lifecycle stage. Telecom apps can segment by plan type, add-on usage, roaming status, or support behavior. E-commerce and food apps can segment by purchase frequency, basket behavior, loyalty tier, or promo sensitivity. Show feature education where it has a stronger chance to change behavior.
Try for free
4/ 
Test the adoption hypothesis before UI work
Low feature usage can come from three different issues: users do not see the feature, do not understand the value, or do not want the action enough. Use in-app campaigns to test these hypotheses before planning interface changes. Validate adoption signals first and invest in development later.
Try for free

Boost in-app engagement! 🚀
Create interactive in-app experiences that help users explore features, understand value, and take action. Build in-app messages, stories and games without code to influence key product and revenue metrics.
FAQ
Why do new app features often get low adoption? 
Low adoption usually comes from one of five issues: users do not see the feature, do not understand why it is useful, see it at the wrong moment, meet friction during first use, or belong to a segment where the feature has weak relevance.
That is why feature adoption campaigns should test more than the message. Teams need to check the segment, trigger, placement, CTA, and first-use flow before assuming the feature itself has failed.
What is the difference between a feature announcement and a feature adoption campaign? 
A feature announcement tells users that something is new. A feature adoption campaign is built around the next product action.
A stronger adoption campaign defines who should see the feature, when they should see it, what value frame they need, which format should explain it, and which action proves progress. For example, opening the feature screen, completing setup, using the feature twice, or reaching a monetized area.
When is the best moment to introduce a feature in-app? 
The best moment is usually a high-intent moment. This can happen when a user opens a related section, repeats the same behavior, reaches a limit, abandons a flow, views an upgrade area, returns to a task, or shows interest in a connected product category. At this point, the feature has context. The message does not interrupt a random session. It explains a better next step while the user is already close to the relevant action.
Which in-app format works best for feature adoption? 
The format should match the complexity of the feature and the type of action you want to drive. Smart banners work well for short prompts and entry points. Stories fit product education and value explanation. Bottom sheets help at moments of hesitation inside a flow. In-app messages can guide users to a specific action. Widgets can collect intent, feedback, or preferences. In-app landings give more space for complex features. 
What metrics should product teams track for feature adoption? 
The right metric depends on the feature’s role. For onboarding features, track first-use completion and activation. For monetized features, track visits to paid areas, upgrade clicks, checkout starts, and conversion. For loyalty features, track enrollment, reward views, point usage, and repeat visits. For support-related features, track self-service usage and changes in support requests. For engagement features, track repeat use, session depth, and return rate.
How can InAppStory support feature adoption? 
InAppStory helps teams build feature adoption campaigns inside the app using stories, smart banners, pop ups, bottom sheets, full-screen messages, widgets, mini-games, and in-app landings. Teams can target campaigns by behavior, lifecycle stage, status, product interest, and previous actions. They can test different value frames, guide users to the right screen, collect feedback, and measure whether users move from awareness to the intended product action.

FAQ
Do you have a free trial? 
Yes. We offer a one-month free trial that starts after your first campaign goes live in the app. That gives your team time to complete integration, prepare the first use case, and test InAppStory on real users instead of losing trial time during setup. The free trial can include the selected products you want to test depending on the agreed rollout plan.
How does the integration process work? 
Our solution requires single integration of SDK with no need for extra coding and can usually be launched within 2 weeks. Once integrated, our platform operates smoothly and does not require further involvement from your development team.
What kind of support can I expect? 
Our support team is here to ensure your success at every step. We offer rapid, hands-on assistance through Slack, email, and personal video conferences, addressing any technical, integration, or customization questions you might have, typically within a few hours. From initial setup to ongoing optimization, our professional support is designed to guide you through every phase of your journey with us, providing the help you need to fully leverage our platform.
How is your platform different from competitors? 
InAppStory brings together three solutions — Stories, Game Center, and In-App Messaging — into one powerful platform for mobile user engagement. You can get a full set of no-code tools to create in-app stories, launch interactive games, and deliver dynamic messages like banners, pop-ups, and modals. Everything is designed to blend seamlessly into your app’s UX, and all plans include unlimited content creation, team access, and advanced analytics with no hidden limits or feature gating.
How do you calculate MAU? 
We calculate MAU as the number of unique users who view stories (story reach) each month, including onboarding stories. For initial estimates, the total app users can be used, but final pricing is determined after integration when we see the actual MAU. This ensures fairness and accuracy.
What app size is the best fit for InAppStory? 
InAppStory usually fits best when an app already has a meaningful active audience, several user scenarios, and an existing marketing or product growth budget.
A common fit is a mobile app with roughly 50,000+ monthly active users, where the team needs to improve onboarding, feature adoption, offers, loyalty, feedback, rewards, monetization, or repeat engagement.
Smaller apps can still be a fit if the use case is strong and the team has a clear plan for in-app communication.
Can we start with one product and add more later? 
Yes. Many teams start with one product, such as stories, in-app messages, smart banners, or game center, and expand after the first use case proves value. The platform is designed as one in-app campaign layer, so additional formats can work together after the initial setup.
Does InAppStory support multilingual in-app stories and games? 
InAppStory allows teams to create in-app stories in any language. Built-in game UI text is available in 12 languages: English, Russian, Arabic, French, Portuguese, Hungarian, Kazakh, Azerbaijani, Uzbek, Spanish, Georgian, and Armenian.
Which languages does the InAppStory support team speak? 
The InAppStory support team assists customers in English and Russian. You can use either language when contacting us about the platform.
What hosting options does InAppStory offer? 
InAppStory supports regional cloud hosting and on-premise deployment. Cloud infrastructure is available in multiple countries, with the hosting location selected based on the customer’s region and project requirements. For organizations with specific security, compliance, or data residency requirements, InAppStory can also be deployed within the customer’s own infrastructure.
Where are InAppStory customers located? 
InAppStory works with mobile teams across Western and Eastern Europe, MENA, Central Asia, and other regions. Our customers include both international companies operating across several markets and local market leaders.
Ready to get started?
